newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU urges Belarus to accept democracy fact-finders.
newsitem.headline: EU urges Belarus to accept democracy fact-finders.

text.p: The European Union urged Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko on Saturday to restore full respect for democracy and accept a fact-finding mission, warning relations would otherwise suffer.

In a statement adopted at a summit in Dublin, EU leaders said they were seriously concerned at developments in Belarus after last month's disputed referendum adopted a constitution greatly widening Lukashenko's powers at parliament's expense.

"The European Council calls on the leadership of Belarus to re-establish full respect for internationally accepted democratic and constitutional principles and practices and hopes that the leadership will accept the Union's proposal for a fact-finding mission," the declaration said.

"The absence of progress in these areas would have a negative impact on relations between Belarus and the European Union, and on Union support for Belarus's accession to the Council of Europe," it said.
The European Parliament urged the 15-nation Union on Thursday to stop financial aid to the former Soviet republic because of doubts over its commitment to democracy.

Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, as EU president, raised the idea of sending a fact-finding mission when he met Lukashenko at an Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) summit in Lisbon on December 3.
EU foreign ministers later endorsed the proposal but there has been no official answer from Minsk.
